test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Identify a structure that plays a role in motility.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Flagella**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Flagella** are long, whip-like structures that protrude from the cell body of certain prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, aiding in cell motility.
 
• They are primarily composed of a protein called **flagellin** in prokaryotes and **microtubules** arranged in a 9+2 arrangement in eukaryotes.
 
• Flagella move in a propeller-like motion to propel the cell through its environment, essential for the locomotion of many bacteria and sperm cells.
 
• In bacteria, flagella can be located at one end of the cell (polar), both ends (amphitrichous), or all over the cell surface (peritrichous).
 
• The rotation of the flagella is powered by a motor protein complex located at the base of the flagellum, driven by the flow of protons across the cell membrane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pili**

 
 
• Pili are short, hair-like structures on the surface of prokaryotic cells that are involved in attachment to surfaces and in conjugation (DNA transfer between cells).
 
• Pili are made of a protein called pilin and are not involved in motility.
 
 
 
• **Villi**
 
 
• Villi are small, finger-like projections found in the small intestine of many vertebrates.
 
• They increase the surface area for absorption of nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Fimbriae**
 
 
• Fimbriae are similar to pili but are typically more numerous and shorter.
 
• They are used by bacteria to adhere to host cells and surfaces, aiding in colonization and infection.
 
 
 
• **Cilia**
 
 
• Cilia are short, hair-like structures found on the surface of eukaryotic cells.
 
• They can move in a coordinated manner to move fluid or mucus over the cell surface or to propel single-celled organisms.
